mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) over 20 trading days signals an easing monetary policy cycle, compressing discount rates and boosting equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) in 60% of FEDFUNDS decline periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Federal Funds Rate (FEDFUNDS) over 60 trading days indicates tightening monetary policy, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: SPX 20d returns remain negative or fail to diverge from baseline (t-test p < 0.05) during FEDFUNDS tightening phases.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) crosses above 6% in a month, risk aversion intensifies, leading to negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns as investors anticipate economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns do not turn negative within 3 months following UNRATE crossing above 6%.

mechanism_narrative: Positive employment growth (PAYEMS) combined with low unemployment (UNRATE <4%) triggers a positive 20-day S&P 500 return through expanded economic activity and consumer confidence.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises >100k and UNRATE <4% in the same month
failure_condition: 20d returns fail to correlate with the combined PAYEMS and UNRATE conditions (R-squared <0.3 over 3-year rolling window).

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (HOUST) and demand (GDPC1) both grow by over 2% in a month, robust demand signals expansion, driving positive 60-day S&P 500 returns through increased corporate earnings and consumer spending.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and GDPC1 both rise >2% in the same month
failure_condition: 60d returns not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p>0.05) during concurrent HOUST and GDPC1 growth periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (HOUST) below 95 for three consecutive months predicts negative S&P 500 5-day forward returns due to reduced economic output and investment.
failure_condition: SPX 5d returns remain positive or fail to diverge from baseline (t-test p <0.05) during HOUST declines below 95.

mechanism_narrative: In a late-cycle expansion regime (UNRATE <4%), a rise in UNRATE above 5% triggers negative S&P 500 20-day returns due to heightened risk aversion and market volatility.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises above 5% in a month during late-cycle expansion
failure_condition: 20d returns remain positive despite UNRATE crossing above 5% in late-cycle regimes (t-test p>0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in personal consumption (GDPC1) and industrial production (HOUST) by over 2% in a month signals robust demand, driving positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns through expanded economic activity.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both rise >2% in the same month
failure_condition: 5d returns fail to correlate with the combined GDPC1 and HOUST growth (R-squared <0.2 over 2-year window).
